**Question 2**. Describe the proportional odds assumption using a
political science example. What are the consequences of estimating an
ordinal logit when this assumption is violated? How do you test this
assumption? Please describe a satisfactory alternative estimation
technique which does not require this assumption.

Question 3. Consider the data described in Question 3. Assume that data
for authoritarian regimes are not included in the data. What problems
might this missing data pose in terms of the model you propose to
estimate (in Question 3). Hint: I strongly encourage you to rely on the
terminology discussed in class and in the course readings. \vspace{1in}

Question 3. You have a dataset with a variable coded 1 if a country
engages in military conflict with another country, 0 otherwise. Your
data includes this measure for 50 years for 25 countries, so
$y_{it}\in {0,1}$. You also have a continuous measure of democracy for
each country, $x_{it}$. Thoroughly describe a model you might use to
estimate the effect of democracy scores on conflict. \vspace{1in}

Question 5.Assume data are censored at $\tau$. Thus,

$$\[y_{observed} = \left\{
  \begin{array}{lr}
    \tau, y_{latent}\leq\tau\\
    \alpha+\sum_K \beta_k x_{k}+\epsilon, y_{latent}>\tau\\
  \end{array}
\right.
\]$$

\noindent \textbf{What are the consequences of this type of censoring? Under what conditions -- if ever -- can censoring be safely ignored?}
\vspace{1in}

\noindent \textbf{Question 6}. What if the value of $\tau$ varies across
units. So,

$$\[y_{observed} = \left\{
  \begin{array}{lr}
    \tau, y_{latent}\leq\tau_i\\
    \alpha+\sum_K \beta_k x_{k}+\epsilon, y_{latent}>\tau_i\\
  \end{array}
\right.
\]$$

\noindent \textbf{How would you estimate a regression model in this circumstance? Elaborate.}
\vspace{1in}

\noindent \textbf{Question 9}. Bayesian methods can easily be
differentiated from frequentistic statistics on theoretical grounds. In
some cases, bayesian and frequentist statistics reach similar results
(the median of the posterior is the same as the frequentist point
estimate). Elaborate on one circumstance on when this occurs.
\vspace{1in}
